Notes: The Chinese Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) provides an early indication each month of economic activities in the Chinese manufacturing sector. It is compiled by China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing (CFLP) and China Logistics Information Centre (CLIC). A higher than expected reading should be taken as positive/bullish for the CNY, while a lower than expected reading should be taken as negative/bearish for the CNY.

The S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index measures the month-on-month change in the number of employees in the manufacturing sector. A higher than expected reading should be taken as positive (bullish) for the USD; a lower than expected reading as negative (bearish).

The ISM Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) measures the health of manufacturing sector based on economic indicators: new orders, inventory and production. A reading above 50 is generally seen as positive for the USD, while a reading below 50 is seen as negative for the USD.

The ISM Manufacturing Prices Index measures the month-on-month change in the price of raw materials and supplier prices paid by manufacturers. Rising prices are generally bearish for the USD while falling prices are generally bullish.

High-profile speeches by Federal Reserve officials are often used by investors to get a sense of the economic outlook and the intentions of the central bank. Market expectations have to be taken into account.

The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the changes in price paid by consumers for goods and services. A higher than expected reading should be taken as positive/bullish for the EUR; a lower than expected reading should be taken as negative/bearish for the EUR.

The Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) shows the number of open jobs in the US. Investors and traders follow this labor market indicator closely to gauge employment and economic conditions.

The Automated Data Processing (ADP) Employment Change measures the month-on-month change in the number of employees in the non-farm private sector. It is an important leading indicator for the official government employment figures.

The S&P Global Services PMI is based on a survey of 400 private service companies. It measures the health of the service sector through economic indicators such as new orders, output, and employment. A reading above 50 indicates growth while below 50 indicates contraction.

The ISM Non-Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) measures the health of the non-manufacturing sector (services) based on economic indicators: new orders, activity, and employment. A reading above 50 indicates expansion while below 50 indicates contraction.

The ISM Non-Manufacturing Prices Index measures the month-on-month change in the price of raw materials and supplier prices paid by non-manufacturing (service) businesses. Rising prices are generally bearish for the USD.

Initial Jobless Claims represents the number of Americans who have filed for unemployment benefits for the first time. High readings generally indicate a weak labor market while low readings indicate a strong labor market.

The Core PCE Price Index measures the changes in the price of goods and services purchased by consumers, excluding food and energy. A higher than expected reading should be taken as inflationary and bearish for the USD; a lower than expected reading should be taken as disinflationary and bullish for the USD.

The Core PCE Price Index measures the annualized changes in the price of goods and services purchased by consumers, excluding food and energy. A higher reading indicates inflation while a lower reading indicates deflation.
